test_title: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 19 Jun, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: As per the Union Budget 2025-26, the start-up incorporation deadline was extended for how many years to avail tax benefits?
solution:
The correct answer is __**5**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• In the Union Budget 2025-26, the government extended the deadline for start-up incorporations by **5 years** to avail of tax benefits under Section 80-IAC of the Income Tax Act.
 
• This extension is aimed at boosting the entrepreneurial ecosystem and promoting start-up culture in India.
 
• The tax benefits allow eligible start-ups to claim a 100% tax deduction on profits for three consecutive years out of their first ten years of incorporation.
 
• The eligibility criteria for start-ups include recognition by the Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT).
 
• This initiative aligns with the government’s flagship **Startup India** campaign to encourage innovation, job creation, and economic growth.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Section 80-IAC of the Income Tax Act**

 
 
• Introduced in the Union Budget 2016, it provides tax exemptions for start-ups recognized by DPIIT.
 
• The tax benefit is available for three consecutive years out of the first ten years of incorporation.
 
• Eligible start-ups must have a turnover of less than ₹100 crore in any of the financial years.
 
 
 
• **Startup India Initiative**
 
 
• Launched by PM Narendra Modi on January 16, 2016, to promote entrepreneurship and innovation in India.
 
• Key benefits include tax exemptions, easier compliance processes, and access to a ₹10,000 crore Fund of Funds.
 
• The initiative also includes programs like the Startup India Hub and the Startup India Seed Fund Scheme.
 
 
 
• **Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT)**
 
 
• A government body under the Ministry of Commerce and Industry responsible for formulating policies for industrial development.
 
• DPIIT recognition is mandatory for start-ups to avail benefits under the Startup India initiative.
 
 
 
• **Economic Impact of Start-ups in India**
 
 
• Start-ups contribute significantly to job creation, with over 8 lakh jobs created by recognized start-ups as of 2023.
 
• They play a crucial role in driving innovation and supporting sectors like technology, healthcare, and renewable energy.
